I use VLC to download Youtube videos.

  • Open VLC
  • Click Media > Open Network Stream
  • Paste Youtube URL into URL box and hit Play.
  • Click Tools > Media Information.
  • Copy link in "Location" box.
  • Paste link in browser and the video will start playing.
  • Right Click > Save video as...

And put whatever file name you want.

You can use this to watch a Youtube video on VLC as well, which gives you the full feature list of VLC, such as slowing down or speeding up the video. HTML5-Beta player on Youtube lets you do that, but the only options are things like 1.00, 1.25, 1.5, etc.

VLC let's you choose any variable, 1.10, 1.20, etc, and find what you prefer (good for long videos like lectures or documentaries or what-have-you).

The resolution defaults to 720p (even if higher ones are available) for me, and I have yet to find a resolution setting to change it.
LPT: You can directly download Youtube videos with VLC Media Player.
